title: Admission retries re-run a full evaluate inside the 20 s dispatch budget shared with the durability fence, so when evaluate plus fence exceed it every attempt fails the same way and the grant expires (2026-10-22 17:46-17:49Z)
outcome: An automatic re-admission adapts to the latency the host is observing instead of repeating a doomed attempt: when an evaluate or the durability fence alone has just exceeded the shared ENGRAM_DISPATCH_BUDGET_MS (20,000 ms, engram_host_adapter.rs:16-27), the next attempt is not started on the same schedule only to be withheld again at the same boundary, a grant issued by a successful evaluate is not left to expire behind a fence wait, and the operator can see why the host is waiting.
acceptance: A measurement note from the running host records, for one held session, each attempt's evaluate, admission-fence and total latency against the 20 s budget and the writer tick state at the time, and names the code path that scheduled the next attempt without regard to the previous attempt's measured latency (engram_admission_retry.rs schedule_engram_admission_retry_locked and the budget clipping in engram_queued_admission.rs:411-421).

With the fix, a still-gated retained head whose typed withheld outcome records exhaustion of the admission-attempt budget is not retried on an unchanged schedule into the same outcome: the host waits for a defined relevant observed condition to clear, uses a bounded documented continuation with verified validity, or holds with a card naming the attempt, measured evaluate (which includes the admission fence), separate fence, total, configured budget and retry condition, without resetting the original head/window. Ordinary proven-unsent fail-open, explicit Refuse/Defer and possibly transmitted operations retain their distinct semantics. For an issued grant whose first Begin is proven never sent, the host promptly attempts exact-owner rebind retirement once under the existing bounded control-call cap, excluding a competing first Begin and without a new Evaluate or timeout/lease inflation; in a deterministic responsive-producer case retirement is confirmed before the producer's authoritative test-clock expiry. Failed, lost or late retirement preserves its exact unresolved identity and never reports released without matching confirmation and durable local settlement. Possibly-sent or restart-ambiguous Begin retains exact replay and cannot be retired from a guessed TTL or status-only inference. Deterministic clock-seam tests cover the responsive, loss, restart, stale-owner and Begin/retirement race cuts, with no synthetic load. No universal use-or-release-before-expiry guarantee is claimed for an expiry-less response during outages or delays.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree with an independent review pair and no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
